judged_text: The sync endpoint's response body (access token plus expiry date per the documented contract) does not contain the ITokenResponse fields (`expires_in`, `refresh_token`) this adapter reads after handleErrorsJson. expiry_date computed from undefined becomes NaN (or stays stale), so the adapter stops refreshing and MS Teams meeting creation fails with expired tokens once the current access token lapses.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`, the token refresh path was changed to call `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. That helper explicitly documents that, when credential sync is enabled, the external endpoint “should only contain the access token and expiry date” and returns the raw `Response`. However, the MS Teams adapter still does `handleErrorsJson<ITokenResponse>(response)` and (per the finding) relies on `ITokenResponse` fields like `expires_in` / `refresh_token`. Unlike other adapters updated in this diff (e.g., Zoom/Office365Calendar/Google) it does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to relax/normalize the expected token shape under sync mode. Given the diff-grounded contract change, any downstream reads of `expires_in`/`refresh_token` will become `undefined` under sync mode and can lead to bad expiry computation / broken refresh behavior.
